summary:
Iran said it is considering a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said, calling the possibility an indication of Iran's good-faith approach. Indirect talks entered a third day as Qatar seeks the release of $6bn in Iranian assets, which could lead to the waterway reopening. Officials from Gulf states are "braced for the worst" as they await Washington's response. On Sunday, Donald Trump repeated his threat to resume strikes on Iran, telling a campaign rally he may have to give Tehran "the hammer".

Binance has begun letting customers withdraw funds after a hack it puts at $6.3bn (£4.7bn), a record. The exchange says 90% of losses are covered, and the FBI blames the North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor. Withdrawals totalled $3.4bn on Sunday after trading reopened, or $3.6bn by another count. A Binance spokesperson said net outflows reached $4.7bn by Monday morning in London.

Authorities in Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert apps were targeted by cyberattacks late on Sunday. In Ukraine, the app sent fake messages warning of a high nuclear radiation danger in Kyiv, while Russia resumed attacks on the southern city of Kherson hours after a ceasefire ended.

headlines.title: Iran considers two-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz
headlines.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said Tehran is considering a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days. Officials from Gulf states are "braced for the worst" as they await Washington's response to the Iranian proposal, during the third day of indirect talks.

headlines.title: Trump threatens renewed strikes on Iran
headlines.summary: On Sunday, Trump reiterated his threat to resume strikes on Iran, telling a campaign rally he may have to give Tehran "the hammer" at some unspecified time. Iran warned that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting.

headlines.title: Binance resumes customer withdrawals after record $6.3bn hack
headlines.summary: Binance has begun letting customers withdraw funds after a hack it puts at $6.3bn (£4.7bn), a record. The exchange says 90% of losses are covered, and the FBI blames the North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor.

headlines.title: Ukraine and Russia report cyberattacks on emergency alert apps
headlines.summary: Authorities in Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert apps were targeted by cyberattacks late on Sunday. In Ukraine, the app sent fake messages warning of a high nuclear radiation danger in Kyiv.

headlines.title: Israeli forces withdraw from Hebron after displacing thousands
headlines.summary: Israeli forces withdrew on Monday from a neighbourhood in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron, ending an operation launched after two Israeli soldiers were killed in late October. Thousands of Palestinians displaced during the raid have begun returning to their homes.

headlines.title: Nine killed as Learjet crashes on Florida street
headlines.summary: A Learjet crashed near a busy road in a residential neighborhood in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called the crash, which happened near President Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort, a "horrific tragedy".

headlines.title: Cyclone Murasu expected to hit Andhra Pradesh coast tonight
headlines.summary: Cyclone Murasu is expected to make landfall tonight between Nellore and Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh, with Chennai and northern Tamil Nadu bracing for heavy rain. At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled at Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam airports.

headlines.title: Armed police begin patrolling Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
headlines.summary: A new police unit armed with military assault rifles has begun patrolling Sydney, an Australian first set up after the Bondi Beach attack last December. The Armed Response Command will deploy at major events and crowded public spaces.
